content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on **Common Text-Processing Problems**. Work through the listed subtopics (Missing and empty strings, Unexpected whitespace, Unicode and encoding considerations, Literal versus regular-expression matching) as decisions in one small data workflow: identify the input and its labels, choose the relevant Pandas operation, then inspect the output shape, values, and types. Do not assume the result is correct solely because the code ran.

import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["", None, "tea"], dtype="string")
print({"missing": int(s.isna().sum()), "empty": int(s.eq("").sum())})

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Avoid assuming inferred types are always correct, treating every repeated record as an error, or overlooking alignment by labels. Check the actual API documentation for the target version and assert the properties that matter to the task.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting a result because the statement ran without raising an exception.
common_mistakes.why: A valid expression can still select the wrong rows, misalign labels, or use an unsuitable dtype.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the output shape, labels, dtypes, and at least one expected value.

common_mistakes.problem: Using the operation without considering missing values or duplicate keys.
common_mistakes.why: Those records may change totals, group sizes, or join cardinality.
common_mistakes.fix: State the policy and test an example containing the relevant edge case.
